title: Sebastian and the Regiment
premise: During the brutal storm year of 1847, widowed lighthouse keeper Casper Ashgrove finds a boy named Sebastian abandoned at her door with a note: forget the face. The child is the illegitimate son of a disgraced officer of the 12th Regiment, and the men who destroyed his father — and massacred villagers abroad to cover it — want no witnesses. Sheltering Sebastian makes Casper keeper of more than a light: she becomes custodian of the dead officer's testimony, hidden in the lighthouse logbook in cipher. As regiment agents close in over one winter, Casper must decide whether a woman with no standing can force an empire's truth onto the record before the ship carrying the official account sails on the morning tide. She succeeds at terrible cost — the truth is read into the parliamentary record, Sebastian is claimed by kin who love him, and Casper, changed forever, keeps the light but no longer believes history happens elsewhere.
about_author: Gideon Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logbooks along the northern coast. This is their second novel, following the acclaimed 'The Salt Ledger.'

chapters.title: The Year of Great Storms
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establishes her isolated life tending the light after her husband's drowning, her belief that history belongs to other people. A supply boat brings news of war and rumors of scandal in the 12th Regiment. Emotional beat: quiet grief and deliberate smallness of life.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. After a ferocious gale she finds a boy, Sebastian, asleep on her doorstep with a note reading 'forget the face' and a sealed oilcloth packet. She takes him in against every instinct for safety. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness cracking open a closed life.

chapters.title: The Oilcloth Packet
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The packet contains a soldier's confession about a massacre ordered by Colonel Vane and ciphered pages keyed to something unfamiliar. Sebastian barely speaks, flinching at red coats. Emotional beat: dread replacing curiosity.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Logbook
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She realizes the cipher matches her late husband's signal-code system; the officer knew him. Deciphered fragments name ships, dates, orders signed by men now decorated heroes. Emotional beat: the past reaching across graves.

chapters.title: Visitors from the Mainland
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Two polite 'inspectors' arrive asking after a missing woman and child. Casper lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. Emotional beat: first taste of complicity and fear.

chapters.title: Sebastian Speaks
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, first time. He recalls his mother, the officer's visits, the night soldiers came. He trusts Casper because she smells of lamp oil like his father did. Emotional beat: trust given like a fragile gift.

chapters.title: What the Light Shows
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A wreck washes ashore carrying a drowned regiment courier and dispatches confirming the cover-up. She hides them in the oil room. Emotional beat: evidence accumulating into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Justice of the Tide
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She weighs giving everything up versus keeping it; a memory of her husband's court-martial injustice surfaces. She resolves to get the record on paper properly. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Neighbors and Nets
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Fishing families become unlikely allies — the widow Marta hides Sebastian during a search, boys run messages. Found family forms around the lighthouse. Emotional beat: warmth amid danger.

chapters.title: The Inspector Returns
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Inspector Hale, less cruel than his partner, hints he suspects Vane himself and offers a dangerous bargain: the packet for protection. Casper refuses to hand over the boy. Emotional beat: moral complexity sharpening.

chapters.title: Fire on the Headland
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Saboteurs burn the boathouse as warning. Sebastian saves Casper's husband's sea chest, proving his courage; the community rallies openly now. Emotional beat: fear answered with solidarity.

chapters.title: The Officer's Widow
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A woman arrives claiming to be Sebastian's aunt — possibly genuine, possibly sent. Casper must judge character under pressure; the woman reveals Vane destroyed her brother, the officer. Emotional beat: alliance forged in shared loss.

chapters.title: Reading the Whole Truth
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The full decipherment: names, dates, the order signed by Vane, and proof the official history was written before the massacre ended. She copies everything in triplicate. Emotional beat: awe and terror at holding history in her hands.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Inn
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. A neighbor sells information for debt relief. Soldiers land at night; Marta delays them with lies and loses her boat confiscated for it. Emotional beat: sacrifice without heroics.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Siege-like hours hiding Sebastian in the lamp room while soldiers search below; the light must be kept burning or ships die. She tends both child and flame. Emotional beat: endurance as defiance.

chapters.title: Hale's Choice
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Ordered to burn the logbook and take the boy, he reads the deciphered pages instead and defects quietly, passing Casper the sailing schedule: the mail ship carrying Vane's official account leaves on the morning tide. Emotional beat: a man choosing conscience over career.

chapters.title: What Must Go to Sea
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The plan: one copy goes with a sympathetic MP aboard the mail ship, one to the Admiralty, one stays hidden. Storms threaten to delay everything. Emotional beat: racing clock tension.

chapters.title: Vane Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The colonel himself arrives, courteous and lethal, offering money and erasure. Casper refuses; he threatens the village. Sebastian steps out of hiding and faces him. Emotional beat: the powerless refusing to be erased.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. In fog and chaos, the copy reaches the mail ship as lines are cast off; Marta's sons row it out through surf; Hale stalls Vane's men. The ship sails with the truth aboard. Emotional beat: breathless triumph.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Weeks later: parliamentary inquiry announced, Vane arrested, Hale testifies. Sebastian's aunt gains guardianship but asks Casper to remain in his life. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly but really.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the inquiry, Sebastian gives testimony; Casper watches from the gallery, a keeper no longer invisible. Her name enters the record beside her husband's. Emotional beat: restoration of voice and dignity.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Light
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, epilogue. A year later, storms gentler, the lighthouse busy with visitors and found family; Sebastian helps trim wicks. Casper writes the true account into the logbook herself. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity remade.
